title: Hahn–Banach and the double dual
summary: Extension of bounded functionals via Zorn's lemma; consequences of Hahn–Banach; the canonical embedding into the double dual; reflexivity.

objectives.description: Prove the real Hahn–Banach extension theorem from the one-dimensional extension lemma and Zorn's lemma.
Construct a norming functional and prove the canonical map into the double dual is an isometry.
Distinguish isometric embedding from reflexivity using c₀ and its duals.

preparation.description: Read Lectures 5–6 (first half) of the 18.102 Spring 2021 notes.

activities.title: Lecture and exact source reading
activities.instructions: Work through the prepared lecture together with its named source sections. Reconstruct the displayed derivations before looking back. The source reading is part of this unit, including the proof obligations identified in the notes.

activities.title: Problem sheet and discussion
activities.instructions: Write an independent attempt at each problem. Use one hint at a time if needed; preserve the original attempt and record what assistance changed. Explain the hypotheses aloud before requesting a step check.

activities.title: Return without the scaffolding
activities.instructions: After a gap, reconstruct the central argument without notes and revisit the transfer or synthesis problem. Compare against your previous work only afterwards. Record what remains unresolved; reading or recall alone does not certify mastery.

activities.title: Proof portfolio: real and complex Hahn–Banach
activities.instructions: Write the complete proof portfolio with the named hypotheses visible. Start independently, use hints progressively, and retain any corrections made after source reading or feedback. Revisit the central argument without notes after a gap.

exitCheck.description: Complete the explicit proof/synthesis task and review the rest of the sheet against all objectives. Each criterion records the particular argument demonstrated; an accepted task does not certify unrelated applications or learning retention.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Hahn–Banach requires the original subspace to be closed.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The extension theorem needs a bounded functional on a linear subspace; neither closedness nor completeness is required. Closedness is needed for positive distance in the separation exercise.

commonMisconceptions.claim: An isometry into the double dual proves reflexivity.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Isometry gives an injective canonical map. Reflexivity additionally requires its surjectivity.
